tickets.title: Reuse native Grok sign-in through Wake
acceptance: Operator can initiate or reuse the official account session through sanitized Wake controls.
Existing native provider authentication obtains credentials over its private command channel; tokens never appear in public status or worker configuration.
Shared refresh honors compatible locking/rotation; logged-out, expired, unknown or incompatible state is explicit.
Readiness distinguishes sign-in, entitlement and usable inference; no silent API-key route.
tickets.progress: Independent integrated source slice accepted. Device login ended without sign-in; no retry. Live proof remains joined qualification, as frozen spec requires.
tickets.validation: Real CLI register/status/private bearer; protected HTTP/native MCP parity; eight focused tests pass. Joined real-account and installed refresh proof remain T8 gates.

tickets.title: Run a Grok coding turn inside Codex
acceptance: A Grok-native provider streams text and fragmented function calls into the existing Codex loop, executes existing terminal/file/MCP tools and continues with their results.
Configuration and remote/native protocol serialization support the Grok-specific transport without re-enabling the removed generic chat provider.
The existing private command-auth interface supplies bearer credentials; session authentication and model routing headers are bound to each request.
Incomplete streams, malformed calls and unknown results cannot become successful completion or repeated tool effects; OpenAI behavior remains compatible.
tickets.validation: Native Grok+2 OpenAI regressions3PASS; API274PASS; remote1PASS; proto byte equal; focused API lint and touched formatting pass; primary19file hashes/patch tree/bundle verified. Joined live/package qualification remains T8.

tickets.title: Retire the superseded separate CLI-worker path
acceptance: Preserve original issue/PR/source, runtime and skill custody plus the original terminal native_auth_required operation.
Reconcile exact task-owned unit/process/profile effects before reversible retirement; partial discovery does not establish quiescence.
Remove only the task-owned idle setup and its misleading installed routing, preserving unrelated skills, native homes, browser Grok and other sessions.
The superseded intake/draft points to the native-provider specification; retirement does not claim native-provider acceptance.
tickets.validation: exact unit absent/inactive PID0; public Grok discovery complete empty/noholds; installed routing hashes match source; original refusal/rollback evidence retained

tickets.title: Select qualified Grok models and accounts
acceptance: A unified native picker and public model operations distinguish qualified, unavailable, stale and unverified choices.
Exact account labels, model capabilities and an explicit validated default resolve one inference selection before work.
Unsupported optional features are individually explained; required-capability failure blocks ready status.
Current OpenAI defaults remain unchanged, and provider/model/account identity is attributable rather than inferred from display labels.

tickets.title: Delegate mixed-provider workers under one allowance
acceptance: An OpenAI parent can explicitly select a Grok worker and vice versa through normal Codex worker controls.
Workers inherit the exact inference selection unless overridden; provider-only Grok requests use the validated account default.
Accepted work pins its selection and retains the original permissions, parent identity and cumulative Wake allowance.
Reported usage is attributable across the mixed tree; missing provider usage remains unknown and cannot grant free work.

tickets.title: Continue across provider or account changes
acceptance: Changing selection during a turn stages the next safe boundary without implicitly stopping work.
Cross-provider or account changes create an automatic linked continuation carrying bounded portable context and completed tool results.
Source history, provider-private state, permissions and cumulative allowance remain preserved and attributable without extra confirmation.
A handoff that cannot preserve required objective/constraints/attribution/allowance holds; resume never replays uncertain actions.

tickets.title: Stop, revoke and recover mixed-provider work safely
acceptance: Stop prevents further owned local tool scheduling and reports provider completion/usage uncertainty separately.
Shared logout/revocation blocks new Grok turns and interrupts only owned Grok work while OpenAI work remains untouched.
Auth/quota/provider failures become actionable held states; authorized parent reassignment is explicit.
Strict-budget work stays held on missing accounting; durable recovery retains unknown actions and does not reset allowances.

tickets.title: Qualify the native-provider release candidate
acceptance: The complete exact native package passes the existing isolated upgrade/rollback, history, multi-client and failed-start gates.
A bounded disposable-workspace workflow verifies real account sign-in/entitlement, streaming coding tools, MCP, mixed workers, handoff, Stop/resume and usage readiness.
Adverse auth/logout checks remain isolated from everyday sessions; no credentials or private histories are copied into fixtures.
Exact source/artifact identities, rollback custody and first-profile activation readiness are recorded; required failures remain blockers.

shared_contracts.auth: Existing ModelProviderAuthInfo command/args, bounded timeout, private stdout bearer token and sanitized stderr; public CLI/API/MCP never return credentials. T1 owns Wake implementation; T2 consumes existing native interface.
shared_contracts.native_events: Grok-specific native wire/remote-config support normalizes into existing ResponseEvent/tool loop; T2 owns this contract.
shared_contracts.selection: Catalog readiness and exact provider/account/model selection from T4, consumed by T5/T6/T7.
shared_contracts.closure_order: Close implementation children from validated integrated acceptance, then one broad review and one bounded remediation. Requalify causally affected exact package after corrections; merge/deploy is a subsequent program stage, not a premature ticket-closure claim.

final exact runtime readbacks and task worktree cleanup
